title: Flight Delay, Denied Boarding & Lost Baggage Compensation in Bangladesh: Montreal Act 2020
metaTitle: Flight Delay & Lost Baggage Rights BD: Montreal Act
metaDescription: How to claim airline compensation for flight delays, denied boarding, or lost checked baggage in Bangladesh under the Montreal Convention Act 2020 & CAAB rules.
keywords: lost baggage compensation hazrat shahjalal airport
heroIntro: Every year, thousands of outbound workers, NRBs, and international travelers flying through Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport (DAC), Chattogram, or Sylhet suffer uncompensated flight cancellations, overbooked denied boarding, or lost checked luggage. Under the Carriage by Air (Montreal Convention) Act, 2020 and the Civil Aviation Act, 2017, passengers flying international routes to or from Bangladesh enjoy enforceable statutory compensation rights—backed by strict written notice deadlines and judicial remedies in Dhaka.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Air Passenger & Baggage Claims in Bangladesh
quickAnswer.text: International flights departing from or arriving in Bangladesh follow the Carriage by Air (Montreal Convention) Act, 2020. Airlines bear strict financial liability for lost, damaged, or delayed checked baggage up to statutory SDR limits, provided passengers file written notice within 7 days for damage or 21 days for delay and sue within two years.

2-Year Limitation Period (Article 35): Civil suit in Bangladesh courts must be filed within 2 years from arrival date

sections.h2: Statutory Framework: Montreal Convention Act 2020 & CAAB Oversight
sections.content:
Bangladesh replaced older Warsaw-era aviation liability limits by enacting the Carriage by Air (Montreal Convention) Act, 2020, incorporating the 1999 Montreal Convention into domestic law alongside regulatory oversight by the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) under the Civil Aviation Act, 2017.

Whenever a ticketed itinerary originates in, terminates in, or includes an agreed stopping place within Bangladesh and another State Party (including the US, UK, EU, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Canada, and Australia), the airline cannot contractually reduce statutory passenger compensation caps below the Act’s limits. Any fine-print airline condition attempting to waive mandatory liability for baggage loss, passenger injury, or unjustified delay is void under the Act, and passengers can enforce claims directly against the carrier’s Dhaka office or GSA.

sections.h2: Damaged, Delayed, or Lost Checked Baggage: Notice Deadlines & Proof
sections.content:
Most passenger baggage claims fail not because the airline is innocent, but because travelers miss mandatory written protest windows under Article 31 of the Schedule to the 2020 Act:

  • Immediate Airport Action (PIR): Before exiting the customs arrival hall at Dhaka, Chattogram, or abroad, report the missing or broken bag at the airline’s Baggage Services counter and obtain a signed Property Irregularity Report (PIR) with your baggage tag number attached.
  • Damaged Checked Baggage — 7 Days: You must submit a formal written claim (email + airline portal ticket) within 7 days from the date you received the damaged bag. Photograph the broken shell, wheel, or torn lock next to the baggage tag sticker.
  • Delayed Baggage — 21 Days: If your suitcase arrives days late and forces emergency purchases of clothing or essential toiletries, submit itemized receipts in writing within 21 days from the date the bag was finally handed over to you.
  • Presumed Lost After 21 Days: Under Article 17(3), if an airline admits loss or fails to locate checked baggage within 21 days of expected arrival, you can enforce full lost-baggage compensation without proving airline negligence. Retain purchase proofs, packing lists, and passport stamps.

sections.h2: Flight Cancellation, Extended Delays & Overbooked Denied Boarding
sections.content:
Under Article 19, a carrier is liable for provable financial damage caused by flight delay (missed non-refundable hotel bookings, onward separate-ticket losses, missed work contracts, or overnight meals and accommodation), unless the airline proves it took all measures that could reasonably be required to avoid the delay—such as unforeseeable severe weather or sudden air-traffic closure rather than routine technical maintenance or crew scheduling failures.

If an airline bumps a confirmed, on-time passenger due to commercial overbooking, passengers are entitled to immediate re-routing or full ticket refund to the original payment method without unauthorized cancellation deductions, hotel accommodation during overnight rerouting, and statutory compensation for financial losses arising from involuntary denial of boarding. Travel agencies or aggregators who withhold airline-approved ticket refunds can also be pursued under Bangladesh contract breach remedies.

sections.h2: How Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) & Travelers Pursue Claims
sections.content:
NRBs traveling from London, New York, Toronto, Riyadh, or Dubai often struggle when airlines ignore emails after landing in Dhaka. To preserve jurisdiction and cross-border enforceability:

  1. Keep Jurisdiction Options Open (Article 33): Under the Montreal Convention framework, a passenger may sue either where the carrier is domiciled, its principal place of business, the place of business where the ticket was bought, the destination, or—for bodily injury or death claims—the passenger’s principal and permanent residence if the carrier operates there.
  2. Serve a Formal Advocate Legal Notice: Before litigating in Dhaka, serving a statutory legal notice on the airline’s Bangladesh GSA (General Sales Agent) and Country Manager with PIR, boarding passes, e-ticket PNR, and itemized receipts frequently triggers an out-of-court settlement within 15–30 days.
  3. Escalate to CAAB & DNCRP: Simultaneously lodge a regulatory grievance with the CAAB Passenger Facilitation wing and, for local ticket-refund or deceptive fee violations, before the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection (DNCRP). Also keep copies of passport and travel records secure in case of airport immigration or offload disputes.

sections.h2: Filing a Civil Suit or Consumer Complaint Against an Airline in Dhaka
sections.content:
If settlement fails, claimants must observe the non-extendable 2-year limitation period under Article 35 (counted from arrival at destination, scheduled arrival date, or date carriage stopped). Ordinary limitation-saving extensions do not revive an expired Montreal Convention claim.

Money suits for unliquidated baggage or delay damages above small-claims thresholds are instituted before the competent Joint District Judge or Senior Assistant Judge Court in Dhaka where the carrier’s regional office operates. Travelers residing overseas can appoint a trusted representative or advocate in Bangladesh via an embassy-attested Power of Attorney and check virtual representation options from abroad so court proceedings do not require another international flight.

faqs.q: How much compensation can I claim for a lost suitcase on an international flight to Dhaka?
faqs.a: Under the Carriage by Air (Montreal Convention) Act, 2020, airlines bear strict liability up to statutory Special Drawing Rights (SDR) limits—historically 1,288 SDR and periodically revised upward by ICAO to 1,519 SDR—per passenger for proven contents value of lost, damaged, or delayed checked luggage, unless you declared higher value at check-in.

faqs.q: What if I left the airport without a Property Irregularity Report (PIR)?
faqs.a: Leaving the arrivals hall without a PIR makes evidence gathering harder, yet it does not extinguish your statutory claim if you immediately email a written complaint with your boarding pass, baggage claim tag sticker, and damage photographs strictly within 7 days for damage or 21 days for delay under Article 31.

faqs.q: Can an airline refuse a cash refund and force me to take a travel voucher after cancelling a flight?
faqs.a: No. Whenever the operating carrier cancels a scheduled flight or enforces a major schedule disruption that renders travel useless, passengers retain the statutory right to demand a full monetary refund back to their original payment card or bank account rather than accepting an expiring restricted airline credit voucher.

faqs.q: Where can NRBs sue an airline if the ticket was bought in the UK or US for travel to Dhaka?
faqs.a: Under Article 33 jurisdictional rules of the Montreal Convention, claimants may choose to sue at the airline domicile, its principal place of business, the ticketing office location where the contract was concluded, or the final destination of carriage—allowing litigation either in Dhaka courts or abroad depending on limitation periods.
